messages:
Alex M: FYI I spun up a canary for nova27b with int8 quant + prefetch window=1024 to validate latency gains. Seeing intermittent OOMs on long chat traces (~context 12k tokens).
Maria G: saw the same in local repro. Error is `RuntimeError: CUDA out of memory` coming from KV cache growth — memory climbs steadily during prefix replay.
Raj P: logs? can you paste the minimal repro and the node id?
Alex M: repro command: `python -m rdinfer.run --model nova27b --quant int8 --prefetch 1024 --batch-size 4 --sequence-length 12000 --prompt-file tests/long_chat.json`
Alex M: node gc dump: `mem_used=42.1GB -> 48.7GB over 40s` before OOM at 49.2GB on a 48GB GPU.
Sophie L: interesting — default max_new_tokens for nova27b can be 1024 in our model catalog right now. That's high for many chat workloads; combined with aggressive prefetch it's likely pushing KV allocations.
Maria G: quick experiment: reduced prefetch window to 256 and batch_size to 2, int8. Memory stabilizes around 38GB and no OOM in 10 runs. Latency hit ~8% but still within SLO for canary.
EvalBot: latest eval run (convQA dev) — baseline fp16: EM=0.78, int8+prefetch1024: EM=0.76, int8+prefetch256: EM=0.755 (noise ~0.01). Quality drop is small but visible for longer answers.
Raj P: two orthogonal fixes: (1) change default_max_new_tokens for nova27b to 256 in model catalog, (2) add adaptive prefetch that scales with sequence length and available mem. Short-term we can flip the default.
Sophie L: +1 for default change as hotfix. We should also add a soft cap enforcement in serving runtime: reject request > default_max_new_tokens for unpinned models or return a warning with suggestion to increase quota.
Alex M: I'll push a canary config: set model.params.default_max_new_tokens=256 and model.runtime.prefetch.window=256 for canary pool. Also enable KV-evict debug metrics.
InfraBot: deploy triggered by Alex M: canary-config-update -> eng-ml-canary-3 (started).
Maria G: after config swap: ran the same long_chat test 25 times, zero OOMs, memory profile stable. Throughput down ~12% but p95 latency still within target.
EvalBot: post-hotfix eval: int8+prefetch256 EM=0.758, conversational coherence metric (winrate) unchanged. No regression alarm.
Raj P: plan: 1) keep canary for 24h with new defaults and metrics enabled, 2) run batch of 500 long-context traces and cost perf job, 3) if stable, roll out default change to hosted catalog, 4) follow-up: implement adaptive prefetch for next sprint.
Sophie L: add a note in model onboarding checklist: test with two prefetched windows (256, 1024) and with max_new_tokens at 256/512 to observe memory knee.
Alex M: noted. I'll also open a PR to catalog with rationale and link to these perf traces. PR will contain recommended runtime knobs: `prefetch.window=256`, `default_max_new_tokens=256`, `prefetch.eviction_policy=LRU-clip`, and escalation steps.
Maria G: can we add a quick server-side guard: if mem_free < threshold and request.new_tokens > 512 then return 429 with message to try smaller max_new_tokens or retry later?
Raj P: yep we have quota/guard infra, I'll file a tiny change to make it model-aware and opt-outtable.
Alex M: thanks — marking this thread resolved for now. Will update after 24h soak and the PR. :thumbsup:
InfraBot: canary-config-update completed (eng-ml-canary-3) at 2003460345.
